newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Mortar fire erupts near Zaire's Lubumbashi city.
newsitem.headline: Mortar fire erupts near Zaire's Lubumbashi city.

text.p: Mortar fire exploded on Monday on the southern approaches to Zaire's second city of Lubumbashi, which has been declared the next main target by rebels, witnesses said.
"It sounds to me like incoming 120 mm mortar fire landing about seven km (four miles) south of the city," a military expert in the city said.
Explosions first erupted around 8.45 p.m (1845 GMT) and were continuing half an hour later, interspersed with the rattle of multi-barrelled rocket launchers.

Residents said they suspected the firing was from Laurent Kabila's rebels who were closing in on the copper mining capital. Earlier in the day a Zaire government army commander said the rebels were about 15 km (10 miles) from the city.
In Kinshasa defence ministry sources said Zaire's Special Presidential Service forces (DSP) had been sent to push back rebels from Kipushi, 30 km (20 miles) southwest of Lubumbashi.
It was not clear if the firing had anything to do with their reported intervention.
Earlier in the day fear gripped Lubumbashi amid reports that rebels had taken Kipushi, which is on the Zambian border.
Shops remained shut and students hurried home from the city centre as the reports spread. There were no taxis and very few other vehicles in the town, where daily life ground to a halt.
The fall of Kipushi could not be directly confirmed, but business people in Lubumbashi said the news had come directly from Kipushi residents contacted by telephone before lines became jammed.

The defence ministry said military authorities arrested about half a dozen soldiers in Lubumbashi in connection with a statement broadcast on local radio ordering troops to lay down their arms in anticipation of the rebels' arrival.
A defence ministry spokesman told Reuters the soldiers involved would be severely punished by the local military high command.
"The soldiers who wrote the communique broadcast on the radio this morning have been arrested," he said.
Asked about the position of the rebels, the spokesman said: "The rebels are said to be on the outskirts of Lubumbashi, but I cannot confirm this report."

The rebels have seized the richest provinces of the vast Central African state since taking up arms in October to topple President Mobutu Sese Seko's 32-year rule. They met little resistance from the poorly paid and demoralised Zairean troops.
